articles.headline: Aston Villa handed toughest festive fixture run as Newcastle get lucky
keyFacts: The Premier League has confirmed the fixture dates and kick-off times for the upcoming festive schedule.
Aston Villa faces the toughest schedule with five games in 16 days, while Newcastle has 20 days to complete their five matches.
Each Premier League club is scheduled to play five games during a 20-day period around Christmas and the New Year.
body: Aston Villa could be in for a Christmas nightmare this festive season while Newcastle have been handed an early gift.
The fixture dates and kick-off times for the hectic top-flight schedule around Christmas and the New Year have been confirmed.
Emery’s Villa have the fewest days rest this Christmas Getty
Full Premier League festive schedule plus kick-off times and TV picks
There are no games on Christmas Eve or New Year’s Eve this season but the full slate of Boxing Day games is back and there is one evening game scheduled for January 1.
As ever, fans will be taking stock of how the powers-that-be have placed their games, with each Premier League club playing five times in a 20-day stretch.
Some have got lucky, with Newcastle getting the full allotment of 20 days to play their matches in.
But others, like Aston Villa , haven’t been so fortunate.
Aston Villa handed tough run
Judging by the number of rest days each club has between the start of Matchweek 16 and the end of Matchweek 20, Unai Emery’s Villa have been handed the toughest test.
The Villans have been scheduled their five games in 16 days, just over a game every three days.
They play the final game of Matchweek 16, travelling to London to face Chelsea on Monday, December 21 at 8pm.
They then host Leeds early on Boxing Day before welcoming Liverpool and heading to Bournemouth either side of the New Year.
The busy Christmas period is nearly upon us again Getty
Villa then complete their five-game run with a trip to Everton on Tuesday, January 5, in the earlier kick-off time of 7:30pm.
Arsenal have the second worst run, hosting Manchester United at 4:30pm on Sunday, December 20 before finishing their festive run by welcoming Brentford to the Emirates at 7:30pm on January 5.
The major caveat with Arsenal’s run compared to Villa’s is that the Gunners do not have to travel.
Mikel Arteta’s side are in London – playing 11 games either home or away – from November 24 right through to January 16 in a strange fixture quirk.
Brighton, Everton, Nottingham Forest and Sunderland also have 17 days between their quintet of games.
Newcastle get lucky
For Villa’s bad luck, Newcastle will be counting themselves fortunate.
Matthias Jaissle’s Toon have been scheduled to play their five games across the full 20 day window.
They begin Matchweek 16 by making the trip to Brentford for the 12:30pm kick-off on Saturday, December 19.
Newcastle’s festive schedule is favourable Getty
They then face Manchester City, Forest and Chelsea around the festive days before heading to Manchester United for an 8pm kick-off on Thursday, January 7.
Man City, Leeds, Fulham and Coventry have also got a good amount of rest days, playing their five games across a 19-day span.
City will be confident of maintaining their title challenge around the festive period.
They have plenty of rest days while facing Hull, Newcastle, Everton, Tottenham and Leeds in a favourable run.

The Baltimore Ravens are preparing for Thursday's game against the Jacksonville Jaguars with one of the NFL's most unusual quarterback situations.
Lamar Jackson suffered a thumb injury during Sunday's loss to Buffalo, while backup Tyler Huntley also was injured during the game.
The Ravens subsequently turned to undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano, who made his NFL debut under extremely difficult circumstances.
With Jackson and Huntley facing significant injury concerns, Fagnano has emerged as the likely starting option for Thursday.
How Baltimore reached this point
Jackson's injury occurred on the opening offensive play against the Bills when his throwing hand made contact with Buffalo defender Greg Rousseau.

Fagnano entered the NFL as an undrafted rookie and began the season well behind Jackson on Baltimore's depth chart.

Kaden Slovis joined the organization after spending time with Green Bay's practice squad, while Austin Reed was added as another potential option.

The Ravens must simplify their approach enough to support whichever quarterback starts.
For Fagnano, the opportunity could become a defining early moment in his career.

articles.headline: Sam Altman says ‘I want you to have so much RAM’ after huge backlash
keyFacts: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman stated he wants people to have plenty of RAM after facing backlash for previous comments about memory usage.
Altman claimed his earlier remarks criticizing home computer RAM usage were taken out of context and that he supports increased memory production.
Analysts suggest that global memory shortages driven by AI data center demands may continue for years despite calls to increase production.
body: - Sam Altman says he wants there to be enough RAM for everyone
- He argues his past comments were taken out of context
- Altman previously criticized people using RAM sticks in their home PCs

When OpenAI chief Sam Altman said that it was “quite terrible” that everyday folks were using RAM sticks in their computers when there wasn’t enough for all the data centers his company wants to build, it went down just as badly as you’d expect. Now, Altman has tried to walk back his comments and say it was all just a misunderstanding.

For full context, Altman’s original remarks were made on the Cheeky Pint podcast, where he said: “From a global allocation perspective, actually, it’s quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world’s limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer… You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you’re trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment. And somehow many people’s intuition is the opposite of that.”

Posting on X, Altman agreed to a user’s request to change his name to “Ram Altman” in reference to his earlier statements. Altman then commented that he would make the name change “but only because I actually do want the world to have tons of memory and people to put as much as they want in their computers, and it is f*cking annoying that this was taken out of context. I have been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time.”
Replying to a different X user who asked “why u want my RAM then,” Altman stated: “I want you to have so much RAM.”
A problem of OpenAI’s own making

Some readers might find Altman’s claim that his quotes from the Cheeky Pint podcast were taken out of context to be somewhat disingenuous. As can be seen in the interview transcript, Altman was speaking about people running local AI models on their computers who might feel that these models are the future and that data centers are unnecessary. It was then that his quote starting “From a global allocation perspective” began.
It’s therefore hard to see his comments as being anything other than a criticism of people having memory sticks in their home computers, because it's bad for data centers.

Part of the problem is that Altman’s own company is one of the foremost reasons why RAM stocks are severely depleted in the first place. The global rush for memory is almost entirely due to the needs of AI data centers, leaving everyday consumers with next to nothing.

Altman’s latest comments will therefore probably do little to endear him in the eyes of PC users — despite his protestations.

articles.headline: FSR 4.1.2 now on Xbox and Xbox handhelds, just in time for a certain big GTA 6-shaped game
keyFacts: AMD updated its Game Development Kit to include FSR 4.1.2 support for Xbox Series X, S, and select handheld devices.
Developers can choose between Full and Lite INT8 upscaling models to balance performance and image quality on Xbox consoles.
This update provides performance optimizations ahead of the upcoming release of Grand Theft Auto 6.
body: With the Xbox Series X and S rapidly ageing, it looks unlikely that the next console generation will be affordable at all. As such, I've been looking at AMD to bring its modern GPU feature set to older hardware to stop me from having to upgrade. It seems it felt my gaze, and Xbox Series X, S, and Xbox handhelds now have FSR 4.1.2 support, which developers can turn on in their games.

AMD has just updated its Game Development Kit with FSR 4.1.2 and two new upscaling models for Xbox Series X and S: the Full INT8 model and the more efficient Lite INT8 model. The Lite one is half the size of the Full one and has a lower upscaling cost. Either console can use either model, but game developers are able to choose which type they implement.

AMD has put out a GDK sample for developers to test, which "switches between the Full and Lite models at runtime, so developers can compare image quality and upscaling cost in the same scene. Upscaler memory is the same for both models because it depends on render and display resolution, not on the model. That makes the choice a performance trade-off, not a memory one."

Interestingly, Ancient Gameplays tested the Lite and Full models two weeks ago and noticed that Lite works better with lower input resolution and even removes some visual noise that is kept in the Full model. They say the "Lite model needs to be more stable because it will be aimed at handheld devices, iGPUs from laptops, and the render resolution on those cases will be way, way lower."

FSR 4.1.2 is also now supported on Xbox handhelds (the top-end ROG Xbox Ally range to start with), though this is seemingly only the one "highly efficient INT8 model", and developers can only get access via Asus' preview driver for the Xbox Ally X and X20. AMD says "it upgrades DirectX 12 games with FSR 3.1 or newer, and ROG Xbox Ally support follows in a later update."

How developers choose to integrate FSR 4.1.2 on Xbox Series X and S will be on a case-by-case basis, but the Lite model being solid certainly suggests good things for future optimisations. And RX 6000 graphics cards got FSR 4.1 early, just a few weeks ago, giving older hardware a little bit more performance.

This is all just in time for a huge launch on Xbox: Grand Theft Auto 6. The game officially launches on November 19, and being a Rockstar game, it's looking like it will be a real graphical showcase. But playing on six-year-old hardware could pose a challenge, so getting an upscaling hand just before the game reaches the starting line surely can't hurt its reception. You won't be able to play the game on Xbox handhelds until the PC port (they aren't really Xbox consoles after all), but I won't be complaining when I'm squeezing a bit more performance out of my Z2 Extreme chip in everything else.

James is a more recent PC gaming convert, often admiring graphics cards, cases, and motherboards from afar. It was not until 2019, after just finishing a degree in law and media, that they decided to throw out the last few years of education, build their PC, and start writing about gaming instead. In that time, he has covered the latest doodads, contraptions, and gismos, and loved every second of it. Hey, it’s better than writing case briefs.

articles.headline: Ronaldo retires from Portugal national team
keyFacts: Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Thursday that he has retired from the Portugal national team after a career spanning over two decades.
Ronaldo made his decision following a falling out with coach Jorge Jesus, who kept him on the bench and planned not to start him.
The Portuguese soccer federation expressed deep gratitude for his service and intends to organize a tribute for him.
body: Lisbon, Portugal — Cristiano Ronaldo announced on Thursday he won't play for Portugal anymore, ending a career that spanned six World Cups and included a European title and the men's all-time international scoring record.

The announcement marked the end of a lauded career that began more than two decades ago before Euro 2004 and finished with him walking out on the national team after a falling out with coach Jorge Jesus.

"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No. 7 shirt of our national team," the 41-year-old Ronaldo said in a long video message on social media. "I never felt it belonged to me alone but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.

"Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart. A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end."

While long-time peer Lionel with Argentina after a much anticipated farewell match last month, Ronaldo's final appearance with Portugal has ended up being on Sept. 24 in a 1-0 win over Wales in the Nations League.

Jesus kept him on the bench for the following match and said he didn't plan to start him in the next one, so Ronaldo decided to leave the team's training camp. Jesus later said Ronaldo would be welcome back and the decision to return was up to him.
The Portuguese soccer federation released a statement expressing "deep gratitude and immense admiration" for Ronaldo's service to the country.

"Cristiano Ronaldo has raised Portugal's profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for many of us, he is the greatest player of all time!" the federation said.
It said it intends to organize a tribute to Ronaldo "in which the fans and the country can one more time applaud and celebrate a player who has given us so much."
Like Messi, Ronaldo will keep playing at club level, and is expected to finish his club career at the end of this season .
He is in pursuit of his 1,000th career goal and has 985. Of those, a record 146 came in 234 appearances with Portugal.
Ronaldo became the first player in his sport to , joining the ranks of the wealthiest athletes, Bloomberg reported in October 2025..

articles.headline: Paul Finebaum blasts College Football Playoff rankings over Alabama-Tennessee controversy
keyFacts: ESPN analyst Paul Finebaum criticized the College Football Playoff committee for ranking Alabama at No. 5 while placing Tennessee at No. 13.
Finebaum argued that Tennessee should be ranked higher than Alabama because they defeated the Crimson Tide earlier this season.
Both teams will play ranked opponents this Saturday, which will provide the committee with more data for future rankings.
body: The first College Football Playoff rankings of the 2026 season have already generated considerable debate, and ESPN analyst Paul Finebaum was among the most outspoken critics.
Finebaum questioned the committee's evaluation process during Wednesday's edition of ESPN's Get Up, taking particular issue with Alabama's placement at No. 5.

The Crimson Tide are 6-2, while Tennessee also stands at 6-2 and defeated Alabama earlier this season. Despite that head-to-head result, the Volunteers entered the rankings at No. 13, eight positions behind Alabama.
Finebaum challenges the committee
Finebaum described the rankings as unusually difficult to understand and questioned the reasoning behind Alabama's placement.
Paul Finebaum rips ‘drunk’ College Football Playoff rankings https://t.co/Ozu9XKPypr
— Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) November 4, 2026
The analyst said Alabama had no business occupying its current position, arguing that Tennessee's victory should carry greater weight in the comparison.
His comments reflected a larger debate about the committee's willingness to prioritize overall résumé strength over head-to-head results.
Alabama's schedule includes several challenging opponents, which may help explain why the committee views the Crimson Tide favorably.
But Tennessee supporters have an obvious counterargument.
Their team defeated Alabama on the field and entered the rankings with the same overall record.
The committee has a different approach
The College Football Playoff committee evaluates several factors when comparing teams, including strength of schedule, results against quality opponents and head-to-head competition.
A head-to-head victory does not automatically guarantee a higher ranking in every circumstance.
Committee chair Hunter Yurachek has explained that direct comparisons become especially relevant when teams are grouped closely in the evaluation process.
That distinction may help explain the eight-place separation between Alabama and Tennessee.
It does not eliminate the controversy.
Saturday offers both teams an answer

Alabama travels to face No. 14 LSU this weekend, while Tennessee meets No. 6 Kentucky. Those games will provide additional evidence for the committee to evaluate before the next rankings are released.
A strong Alabama victory could reinforce its current position. A Tennessee victory over another highly ranked opponent could strengthen the Volunteers' argument for moving up.
Finebaum's criticism has added another prominent voice to a debate that will likely continue throughout November.
Ultimately, the teams still have opportunities to influence their own positions.
But the first rankings have already established one of the season's most controversial comparisons.

Today's top stories

Democrats won this week in districts and states that President Trump carried by double digits just two years ago. The party now has its largest Senate majority since the passing of the Affordable Care Act during Obama's early presidency. Senate results from Alaska and Mississippi are still pending. If those races favor Democrats, their majority could grow to 54, plus the two independents who caucus with them.

- 🎧 A few tight House races remain uncalled, but the swing toward Democrats already rivals the post-Nixon Watergate backlash, NPR's Tamara Keith tells Up First. She highlights two notable race surprises that happened this week. One was in Nevada's 2nd District, which has been Republican since the 1980s. Democrat Teresa Benitez-Thompson claimed victory overnight. The other was in Alabama's 2nd District, where Shomari Figures overcame redistricting that favored Trump by 14 points. Figures won by more than seven points.

- ➡️ Mike Johnson plans to step down as top House Republican in the new Congress after a tough defeat for his party, according to a source familiar with his plans who was not authorized to discuss them publicly.

- ➡️ Voters in 39 states, Washington, D.C., and the Northern Mariana Islands decided on 146 ballot measures covering issues like taxes, transgender rights, traffic cameras and data centers. Here's a summary of the results.

For more than a year, Democrats urged voters to elect them to lower costs and eliminate corruption. Now, the party must act to fulfill its campaign promise. The new Congress is unlikely to see much major legislation signed into law, but Democrats plan to launch ambitious investigations in the House and Senate. Democratic Party leaders and political analysts shared their insights with Morning Edition on the midterm election results, discussed the impacts of mid-decade redistricting efforts and outlined the party's next steps.

- 🎧 Most legislation still requires 60 votes to pass the Senate, and Trump has fluctuated between saying he will be Mr. Veto and expressing willingness to work with Democrats, NPR's Sam Gringlas says. Democrats are interested in restoring enhanced ACA health subsidies, reversing Medicaid cuts, asserting control over tariffs and pushing to end the war with Iran. Gringlas says this election has intensified pressure on Democrats. He points to a voter he met this summer, who said that if Democrats gained control, they would have to enact real changes, otherwise it wouldn't matter who they nominated for president in 2028.

Trump focused on his East Wing ballroom construction project during his first public appearance after the Republicans lost the House and Senate. When asked about the election, he said he wasn't to blame for his party's losses.

- 🎧 Trump quickly pointed out that he wasn't actually on the ballot, NPR's Emily Feng says. But he did urge voters to imagine he was. Voters associated his signature policies, like tariffs and the war in Iran, with rising inflation and gas prices. After Vice President JD Vance posted on social media yesterday suggesting that the war in Iran contributed to GOP losses, Trump somewhat agreed. The president cited its impact on pump prices, but doubled down on the war, saying he would act the same way again if he had to. With a Democratic Congress, Trump will encounter greater legislative gridlock, and Democrats could wield stricter funding controls on issues like immigration enforcement and the ongoing conflict in Iran, Feng says.

- ✉️ Save important documents like birth certificates, passports, product manuals, tax papers and medical records. Choose a method that suits your habits: alphabetize, color-code or simply label. For easy access, place vital documents in a brightly colored folder.

- ✉️ You don't need to shred everything that has your name and address on it. The Federal Trade Commission advises destroying documents containing sensitive information, such as account numbers, birth dates, passwords, signatures and Social Security numbers, to protect against identity theft.

articles.headline: Trump takes 500 actions to weaken cancer protections, new report says
keyFacts: A new report alleges the Trump administration has taken more than 500 actions to dismantle federal protections against carcinogens.
Changes include altering scientific risk assessments, delaying regulations on substances like asbestos, and cutting research staff.
The Guardian contacted the White House and the EPA for comment regarding the report's allegations.
body: Amid a surge in early onset cancer, the Trump administration has taken more than 500 actions to systematically dismantle protections against carcinogens once in place across the federal government, an October report alleges.

The Natural Resources Defense Council report, and comments from current and former officials from the Environmental Protection Agency, bring into focus how myriad changes in federal rules or protocol will dramatically increase the public’s exposure to carcinogens. These are taking effect at a time when some forms of early onset cancer are spiking by about 30% per decade.

Some of the changes have drawn widespread outrage and backlash, including the administration delaying new protections around asbestos, or siding with Bayer in its fight to keep the carcinogenic pesticide glyphosate on the market.

But most changes lie in the nuts and bolts of the federal government. These include alterations to important scientific processes that determine the level of risk people face in exposure to carcinogens. With a few minor adjustments, once-problematic levels of exposure to carcinogens, like formaldehyde, are no longer considered a danger in the federal government’s eyes.

Other actions include the elimination of protective regulatory rules, the exploitation of presidential exemptions for polluters, the delay of new regulations already in motion, the elimination of research funding and wide-scale cuts to cancer research staff.

The actions amount to a “pro-cancer” agenda, the report states. NRDC lead author Erik Olson said he was “surprised by the breadth of the whole government effort to undermine all the protections against cancer”. It is not just the EPA, Olson said, but the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration, independent commissions and many other governmental entities.

“The vast majority of people have no idea that this is happening because the Trump administration is mostly doing it without a lot of fanfare, so it’s hard to piece together this jigsaw puzzle, but we did and it shows a stark and shocking picture,” Olson said.

Officials estimate there will be more than 2m US cancer diagnoses this year. People younger than 50 years old have experienced a nearly 3% increase in colon cancer rates each year from 2013 to 2022. More broadly, rates for 14 types of common cancers have jumped in recent decades, including a 35% increase in childhood leukemia.

The situation calls for more protections, but those rules, regulations and scientific processes that are most essential have long been on industry’s hit list, said an EPA employee who declined to use their name for fear of retribution. Former industry officials are now running the EPA, and it is “horrifying to watch it all play out,” the employee said.

“It is coming from the top [of the agency], and they are being methodical, and doing a lot of damage to these very critical protection points, which is exactly what the chemical industry has wanted,” the employee said. “There is no way to sugarcoat what is happening.”

Among the most widely reverberating changes is the shift away from the “no safe level of exposure” principle that guided EPA science in developing protections for carcinogens. This works by assuming any level of exposure to carcinogens presents a risk, and the risk grows as the exposure dose grows.

The Trump EPA has started implementing a “threshold” approach in which it determines that some exposures to carcinogens is safe. This change has already resulted in weaker protections against formaldehyde, a toxicant widely used in consumer goods. The administration appears to be taking a similar approach to its regulation of hexavalent chromium, a widespread water contaminant.

Nuclear regulators are also eliminating the obligation to reduce exposure to radioactive carcinogens to the lowest reasonably achievable level, despite decades of scientific evidence that any level of radiation poses a cancer risk, the report states.

David Fotouhi, the second in command at the EPA, wrote in an early 2026 memo that the agency had been too conservative in estimating toxic chemicals’ health risks, including carcinogenity. Those values should be revisited and loosened, Fatouhi suggested.

This undermines work on 500 risk assessments done since 1985 by the Integrated Risk Information System (Iris), the small EPA office that determines chemical toxicity. The changes to risk assessments are among the most pernicious Trump EPA moves because the findings underpin regulations that protect people from carcinogens in the air, water, consumer goods and elsewhere, said Betsy Southerland, a former water office director at the agency.
The change to the threshold approach is part of that, and the agency is also targeting a mechanism that protects children by factoring in an increased risk in their exposure to chemicals.

“This is a killer for any emerging contaminant work, and for [carcinogens and other chemicals] that they are revisiting,” Southerland said. The changes could also weaken cleanup requirements at Superfund sites, which is the designation for the nation’s most polluted areas, many of which contain cancer-linked substances.

The Trump EPA quietly loosened guidance around the type of studies required to set regulations around carcinogens, the report alleges. Long-term human or animal studies are the norm, but the agency now uses short-term modeling studies called new approach methodologies (Nams) that are known to be unreliable and easy to manipulate. A Nam study was used to weaken the risk assessment for p-DCB, a widely used consumer chemical that most regulatory agencies label a carcinogen.

Trump has also dramatically increased the use of “presidential pardons” for carcinogenic air pollution, which the report claims will increase exposure to arsenic, ethylene oxide and similar carcinogenic chemicals.

Meanwhile, the agency appears to be systematically using stall tactics via multiple channels to grind the regulatory process to a halt. For example, it delayed requirements for industry to provide cancer data for carcinogenic chemicals like benzene, bisphenol A and vinyl chloride, the building block for PVC material, which were supposed to be reviewed during the administration. It is unclear when this will happen.
Olson likened the situation to someone “dumping a huge dump truck full of termites on your house”.

“It’s not like any one termite is causing the house to collapse, but this is a totally intentional strategy of having innumerable termites eating away at the foundation of all our protections, and the house is going to collapse,” Olson said.
The Guardian has contacted the White House and the EPA for comment.

articles.headline: Suicidal saviorism: Why 60% of Michigan Jews voted for an antisemite
keyFacts: Early exit polling indicates that 60% of Michigan Jewish voters supported a candidate who campaigned on anti-Zionist rhetoric.
Author Sarah Kendis argues that this voting pattern reflects historical political loyalties, complacency, and a failure to prioritize community safety.
The article asserts that Jewish voters must abandon outdated partisan habits and actively prioritize their own security against antisemitic threats.
body: Sixty percent. That’s how many Michigan Jews early exit polling reveals voted for a candidate who not only couldn’t passively condemn Jew-hate from peers, but actively campaigned on sinister rhetoric himself. That’s how many Jews willingly, even enthusiastically, participated in sending the first explicitly anti-zionist Senate candidate to Washington.
In a word: oy.

This is not without precedent, as we all witnessed with the one in three Jews who chose New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani as their mensch one year ago. And, sadly, this will not be the last of such unkosher decision-making, given that two-thirds of Jews still continue to vote blue in national elections as a whole. For those not blinded by membership in any particular party, it was extremely easy not only to imagine this outcome but also to literally see it coming to fruition. So the horror and confusion at this ironic yet inevitable outcome warrant a deeper examination, as this entire debacle may just sum up the politically handicapped state of American Jews today.

It’s true that American Jews have historically trended left due to previously shared values, and it’s true that many continue to cling to the withering shell of what it once may have been, still assuming the fiction that the left is the only side fighting for “humanity”… despite an overwhelming mountain of evidence screaming otherwise. If there is any dark humor to be found, it is the very opposite of “enlightened liberalism” that it took the completely unavoidable to bring people to the already-existing, longest-standing reality. And it is a far greater admission of one’s own hand in promoting regressive politics over the years than yet another pathetic politician openly showing his.

This is exactly what the future of the left looks like, at least until enough of its own can start prioritizing concrete necessities over synthetic labels. Many Jews have now seen it playing out for the past few years, and those of us involved in fighting other parallel ideologies have seen it happening for much longer. The problem is simply that what is recognizably untenable for some continues to be extremely attractive to more.

For better or worse, the left generally seems to be on a suicidal trajectory, and we can and should admit that too many in our diaspora Jewish community are complicit in supporting this harm, creating a blue-tinted Jewicidal path of their own.

There is, of course, the eternal issue of “self-hating Jews,” as seen from Michigan’s own circus of schmucks who willingly supported Abdul el Sayed’s anti-Zionist platform to their own future detriment. This is obviously not difficult in the least to imagine there or anywhere, considering that everyone has their own local contingent who continues to happily support destructive ideas and the bad actors who sell them…not even including the laughingstock of the “Jewish” Voice for Peace front, which has produced an entire cult off of such meshugaas.

But the bigger problem seems to be the issue of self-harming Jews, those who cling to outdated titles and movements out of nostalgically misguided pride or deep longing for identity, helping to enable these very outcomes by enabling overlapping, detrimental ideology… somehow either obtusely overlooking or deliberately defending that the Venn diagram of such issues is always nearing a full eclipse. Yet past and present demonstrate that it will always come back to bite one in the tuchus, and if one still thinks such ideological issues aren’t interwoven after a three-year crash course, one has either chosen pathetic hypocrisy or complete oblivion.

However, perhaps the greatest problem of all is pure complacency and removal from reality. The reality that too many don’t have an accurate reading of political temperature and truly assume that such failures can’t happen. The reality is that too many still consider this a negligible fringe nuisance of their wing, not a core infection of the mainstream.

None of this is to blame Jews for depressing political outcomes, as we’ll always be grossly outnumbered compared to the rest of the populace. However, I still tend to have higher standards for us (despite quite a few desperately intent on proving that such standards are woefully misplaced), and actions or lack of action over time cannot be denied.

This Senate race did not take place in a vacuum. It is a result of years of allowing objective reality to lapse and of feeding subjective fantasy, a refusal to leave the safe comfort of partisanship for the uncomfortable necessity of critical thought. And now these decisions have begun to hit home heavily for this community.

Jews as a whole must, in real life, start actively treating and handling threats with the respect and gravity that we easily give them in their equivalent online. Jews as a whole must do diligent homework on every candidate, protest, organization, and kumbaya-handholding in the false name of “tikkun olam” to see what else they are truly supporting beneath the slick slogans and pretty packaging. Jews as a whole must stop prioritizing personal aspirations and suicidal saviorism over deeper needs so that we are not hurt as a whole.

Jews have long fought for many others due to past shared values and goals, and it is a sad reality that through historically necessary assimilation, Jews also learned a bad habit of tempering our specific suffering to that of all others, to prove our humanity against the antisemitism that insists we have none. That is no longer a working survival method, and our reality is more than enough on its own. Our intangible fears and our tangible targeting are enough to put first. To be very frank, so many others don’t take us seriously precisely because so many of us don’t take ourselves seriously.
ELEVENTH-HOUR ELECTION INTERVENTIONS

Until Jews everywhere start realizing that luxury beliefs have real-world implications, nothing will change. Until Jews everywhere start marching and protesting for themselves before doing so for others, things will stay the same. Until Jews everywhere start putting their own interests equal to and above others’, and show more interest in demanding that we stand up for ourselves over asking when others will stand up for us… well, you know.

All of our enemies, from loud and proud, to pathetically apathetic, to true wolves in sheep’s clothing, won’t be changing anytime soon, so it’s all the more reason for us to do so. Give them all some real chutzpah to take seriously. We simply can no longer afford to not only accept crumbs from others, but crumbs from ourselves.

Sarah Kendis is an oboist and writer in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. A proud Jew and radical feminist, she writes and speaks about antisemitism and women’s issues in the world today. Her work has been published in sp!ked , Skeptic , the American Spectator , and the Federalist .

articles.headline: California’s wealth tax fails — but the damage remains
keyFacts: California voters have rejected a proposed one-time 5% wealth tax on billionaires that supporters estimated would generate $100 billion for healthcare.
Governor Gavin Newsom and economists warned the tax would drive wealthy residents to states with lower taxes, resulting in long-term revenue losses.
Research indicates that seven billionaires have already left California, potentially costing the state billions in annual income tax revenue.
body: California is a stronghold of the American Left. Yet even there, a wealth tax on billionaires appears to have been rejected by voters .

The tax was supported, among others, by economists Gabriel Zucman and Emmanuel Saez, who have been campaigning for higher taxes on large fortunes for years. The proposal called for a one-time tax of 5% on billionaires’ wealth . Around 200 individuals would have been affected. The decisive criterion was residency as of Jan. 1, 2026.

Supporters promised revenues of around $100 billion, supposedly to be spent on healthcare — that always sounds good. Left-wing Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-VT) supported the initiative. He has been railing against billionaires for years, even though he himself is a multimillionaire. His demand: there should be no billionaires at all.
Yet even Gov. Gavin Newsom (D-CA) opposed the one-time levy. He warned that billionaires could leave California, taking their future tax payments with them.
The campaign against the rich began years ago

The vote was merely the latest stage in a development that began much earlier. For years, the rich have been vilified in California: anyone who is particularly successful and has accumulated substantial wealth is expected to pay for it.

A wealth tax was already being discussed in California in 2020. Further proposals followed. Yet the state already has some of the highest income taxes in the United States. The top rate is 13.3%, on top of federal taxes. In Texas or Florida , by contrast, there is no state income tax at all.

The most famous entrepreneur to leave California was Tesla CEO Elon Musk . He moved to Texas in 2020. With its obsession with regulation, California had managed to drive away the greatest entrepreneur in the world. He later relocated important business operations to Texas as well, where, however, a Democrat has now won for the first time since 1988, even though Musk supported the Republican candidate with large sums of money. The state that became wealthy thanks to its entrepreneurs and technology companies is making it increasingly difficult for them to stay.
Seven billionaires with $540 billion in wealth
The new wealth tax initiative gave the exodus additional momentum. The most prominent cases included Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, as well as investor Peter Thiel.

Economists Benjamin Jaros and Joshua Rauh examined the potential consequences of the proposed tax in a study published in October. According to their research, seven billionaires had left California or taken steps to relocate. Together, they held around $540 billion in wealth. That represents almost 30% of the billionaire wealth that was originally supposed to be taxed.
How $100 billion can turn into a loss

According to their calculations, taking into account the exodus and potential legal disputes, the tax would have generated only $28 billion to $36 billion, averaging around $30 billion — instead of the $100 billion forecast by its supporters.

But billionaires do not just pay a one-time wealth tax; they also pay income taxes every year. According to estimates by the two economists, California’s billionaires collectively pay between $3.3 billion and $5.8 billion in state income taxes annually. Under their model, the departure of billionaires could cost California between $1 billion and $3.5 billion in income tax revenue every year in the future.

The researchers therefore calculated not only the potential revenue from the wealth tax but also the long-term tax losses. Assuming the revenue losses persist indefinitely, they arrive at a negative fiscal net present value of $38.9 billion. In 85% of their simulations, the fiscal balance for the state would have been negative.
The rich can leave — everyone else stays

Leftists repeatedly claim that taxes on the rich can be raised sharply without causing them to leave. The experience of European countries, however, shows that high taxes on wealthy individuals can lead to emigration. In France, following the announcement of a 75% top tax rate, the number of emigrants with annual incomes above €300,000 rose by 46% in 2013. In Norway, after the wealth tax was increased to as much as 1.1%, a total of 515 wealthy individuals, each with assets exceeding 10 million kroner, left the country in 2022 and 2023 alone — more than twice as many as before. In Britain, following the abolition of tax privileges for wealthy foreigners, a net loss of 16,500 millionaires was forecast for 2025, compared with 10,800 the previous year.

The barriers in the U.S. are much lower because there is no language barrier as there is in Europe. Anyone living in California can move to Texas or Florida, where there is no state income tax. Of course, when a billionaire moves, that does not automatically mean that their companies and all those jobs disappear as well. But future income tax payments may benefit another state.
BELTWAY CONFIDENTIAL — YES, JD VANCE: LOSING THE MIDTERMS WAS ‘WORTH IT’ TO PREVENT A NUCLEAR IRAN

California’s example demonstrates something else: it is not only a tax itself that can cause damage, but also the years of political campaigning for it. Anyone who constantly stirs up resentment against the rich and demands ever more taxes should not be surprised when they eventually leave.

The Nov. 3 vote has stopped the wealth tax for the time being. But many billionaires had already left before then. Supporters wanted to make the state $100 billion richer. In reality, years of campaigning may have contributed to California permanently losing billions in tax revenue. The rich can leave. Everyone else has to foot the bill.

Rainer Zitelmann is a historian, sociologist, and multiple bestselling author, whose books include Hitler’s National Socialism , The Power of Capitalism , and In Defense of Capitalism: Debunking the Myths . He has published 32 books, which have been translated into 35 languages. His latest book is New Space Capitalism: The Entrepreneurial Path to the Stars .

articles.headline: Agility is the first pure humanoid robot company on the stock market. Are you buying?
keyFacts: Agility is becoming a publicly traded company through a reverse-merger SPAC transaction to raise $465 million in new capital.
The company plans to use the funding to support its new Digit 5 robot, which has $300 million in planned contracts from 30 customers.
CEO Peggy Johnson stated that prototypes of the Digit 5 will be demonstrated at CES 2027 and become widely available by the end of 2027.
body: Almost a year ago to the day, Figure AI CEO Colby Adcock responded to some gentle social media taunting from rival robotics company Agility with a prediction: “You’ll be bankrupt in <12 months.”

Instead, Agility is going public through a reverse-merger that will see it become a publicly-traded company and raise $465 million in new capital from retail investors and a tranche of private funding. The transaction will take place through a special purpose acquisition company, or SPAC.

“You don’t see a lot of dancing robots or backflipping robots from Agility,” CEO Peggy Johnson told TechCrunch ahead of the company’s market debut. “We stuck to our strategy, which [are] these manual, very repetitive jobs, that it’s hard to find humans to do.”

Agility predates the recent boom in physical AI investment. The company was spun out of Oregon State University in 2015 by a group of researchers who made headway in figuring out how to get a robot to walk safely on two legs. The company has focused on deploying a handful of its Digit robots in industrial settings with nine different customers, including Schaeffler, GXO, Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada, and Mercado Libre. Digits are generally used to move heavy totes, including more than 100,000 of them at a GXO logistics facility.

Compared to humanoid robots built by Figure, Tesla, 1X, or Boston Dynamics, Agility’s Digit can seem plodding, but the robot is actually doing real work, and earning money — albeit just $174,000 in the first six months of 2026, and mostly from related parties. The company lost $362 million in the same time period, which means the clock is ticking for it to successfully deploy its infusion of new capital.

The good news is that Agility has $300 million in planned contracts from 30 customers for its new generation of robot, Digit 5. The new model can safely operate around humans, not just in an isolated work cell like its previous model (and indeed most humanoid robots). That deal was “one of the driving factors” behind the decision to take the company public, Johnson said, but could not yet reveal who the customers or say if they are investors.

To close the deals, Johnson said that Digit 5 will have to hit undisclosed targets along several metrics, including throughput, uptime, and accuracy of placement. The company has yet to show off the prototypes of Digit 5, but Johnson said they will be demonstrated at CES 2027 and widely available at the end of that year.

The company’s pitch is that a robot can save $100,000 a year for companies under a robot-as-a-service model and even more if the customer purchases the robot outright. Whether those unit economics work out in the end will depend on Digit 5’s capabilities, both in terms of task accuracy, and how long it can work without pauses for recharging or maintenance.

Johnson gave the example of a single person lifting a 50-pound object — an informal threshold some workplaces use to avoid injury. “Digit can do that over and over and over,” she said. “You don’t want to give a human that job. You want to give that to the robot.”

Agility faces two key questions: How quickly can it find new customers for Digit 5, and how quickly can it improve on the robot’s capabilities? Prospective customers need to spend $500,000 for Agility to do an on-site proof of concept before a deployment is fully scaled up; there were four customers signed up in May, 2026. And while Agility can pick up heavy loads and place them with 98% accuracy, it still — like most of today’s robots — lacks the ability to do complex manipulation tasks.

It’s still not clear how quickly generative AI techniques will unlock the kind of dexterity that could allow robots to handle a wide variety of items. Training systems based on video and teleoperation data have not led to reliable general autonomy, though adapting the transformer architecture to different modalities appears promising to physical AI researchers.

“There’s no internet of physical data of robot movements, and that’s why you see so many people trying to simulate the data using a variety of things, and we use all of those techniques as well,” Johnson said. “They have their pros and cons, but we also have … 65,000 hours of real operational data from real customers in real facilities…that helps us accelerate the training of Digit.”

Johnson said the capital raised in the SPAC transaction would meet the company’s current needs, but wouldn’t project that it would be sufficient for the company to be self-sustaining. She wouldn’t share production targets for Digit 5, but the company has said its production facility could produce 10,000 of the robots annually.

“What you’ll see from us going forward is continuing to listen to our customers, understanding what they need in these facilities,” she said. “We’re taking our cue from them because we’re building a business.”
For all the open questions, Agility still finds itself further ahead of most humanoid builders by dint of simply putting its product in the field.

“Let’s start with the bins and the totes, and then let’s do the picking and the kitting,” cofounder and CTO Johnathan Hurst told TechCrunch at the opening of the company’s Fremont R&D facility this summer. “And then let’s like start working on cardboard, which is really hard, and loading and unloading tractor trailers and things like that. Okay, now we’re at 100 million robots, you know? A trillion-dollar company.”

articles.headline: Pioneering Jewish academy opens in Germany
keyFacts: The first Jewish Academy in Germany has opened in Frankfurt to serve as a center for education, dialogue, and contemporary Jewish life.
Central Council of Jews president Josef Schuster described the institute as a milestone that demonstrates the community's determination to call Germany home.
The 40-million-euro project includes significant security measures, which directors noted reflect the current reality of threats against Jewish institutions in Germany.
body: The western city of Frankfurt was a very conscious choice of location for the new academy, which is the first of its kind in Germany. Frankfurt has traditionally been a hub of Jewish intellectual life — still one of the most important centers of Jewish life in Germany today alongside Berlin, Munich and Düsseldorf.

Less than a 10-minute walk from the city's biggest synagogue, the Jewish Academy is also within sight of the historic festival hall building on Frankfurt Trade Fair grounds where the Nazis herded Jewish men in 1938 and deported them to concentration camps.

It was also here that the Central Council of Jews in Germany was founded in 1950; Berlin serves as its headquarters today. Frankfurt is also home to the Central Welfare Board of Jews in Germany (ZWST) and a Jewish museum that opened in 1988.
Jewish thinkers have played a key role in Frankfurt's intellectual and academic history. The city's Jewish community contributed to the establishment of Goethe University in 1914.

Another important legacy is the Jewish Lehrhaus (house of study). Founded in 1920, it quickly gained prominence and is today associated with the philosopher Franz Rosenzweig (1886–1929). It was closed by the Nazis in 1938. The new academy sees itself in the tradition of Rosenzweig's Lehrhaus.
A place of education and dialogue
Speaking at the opening ceremony on Monday, Josef Schuster, president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, stressed: "We must combat hatred with education, education and more education."

Schuster said the institute was a "milestone” that represented the "Jewish community's determination to call Germany home." At the same time, he emphasized: "Jewish life in Germany is under greater threat than it has been since the crime against humanity that was the Shoah."
German President Frank-Walter Steinmeier also underlined the need to reject antisemitism "outright and without reservation." He added that it must also be combated politically.

The federal president said the murder of six million Jews in the Holocaust had also targeted the Jewish world of learning and knowledge. He specifically honored Rosenzweig's legacy: "This place of knowledge and dialogue was a source of hope, something exciting and something new."
A bridge between tradition and modernity, as well as academia and the general public
The Jewish Academy combines traditional features of a 110-year-old turn-of-the-century German villa with a four-story modern structure, bringing together old and new, history and modernity.
"We see ourselves as a place where the past, present and future are all explored in equal measure," Sabena Donath, the institution's director, told DW.
Donath and her co-director, Doron Kiesel, view the academy as "a bridge between academia and the general public" and as "a home for scholars and a home for those who ask questions."
Donath said the aim was to put the focus on topics related to the philosophy of religion and ethics as well as on topical debates concerning contemporary Jewish life.
The program aims to reflect the many facets of Jewish life and the diverse forms of Judaism.
Kiesel told DW: "We want to show how Jews live today and how heterogeneous Jewish life is. And that it is completely wrong to speak of 'the' Jews or 'the' Jewish way of thinking."

Ahead of the opening, the president of the Central Council of Jews also named interfaith dialogue as one of the institution's topics, and, in an interview with the German newspaper, the Frankfurter Allgemeine, Schuster expressed the hope that the academy would bring into the public sphere "Jewish themes besides the topic of antisemitism and Jewish persecution.”

But these issues will also be on the agenda. "We have,” said Kiesel, "a problem in this country that antisemitism is concealed behind numerous topics, but keeps on resurfacing, sometimes more evidently, sometimes more subtly.”

The project grew out of an initiative from the former head of the Central Council Dieter Graumann, who encouraged the setting up of an educational department in 2012. Its work was shaped by the directors of the new institution.
Security measures push up price tab

A mezuzah — a small capsule containing verses from the Torah intended to serve as a reminder of God's commandments — is affixed to the entrance of the academy. Security measures are also an integral part of this new building.

"It is a bitter reality that Jewish institutions must be guarded," said Donath. The academy is being protected just as Jewish schools and synagogues must be protected. "For us, this is a sad reality of everyday life."

The construction costs of around €40 million ($45 million) — about half of which was covered by the Central Council of Jews and half by the federal and state governments — ended up being significantly higher than calculated at the groundbreaking in 2021, partly due to the structural security measures.

articles.headline: Nintendo game sales surge thanks to Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream, but Switch 2 hardware suffers big decline
keyFacts: Nintendo reported a 37.4 percent decline in Switch 2 hardware sales during the first half of the current fiscal year.
Software sales increased significantly, driven by the popularity of Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream which sold 8.81 million units.
Nintendo maintains its forecast to sell 16.50 million Switch 2 units by the end of the current fiscal year.
body: Nintendo's latest financial earnings report is here, revealing healthy software sales thanks to the enormously popular Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream. Sales of Switch 2 hardware, however, are down.

As per Nintendo's 2nd Quarter fiscal earnings report, focusing on the three-month period ending 30th September 2026, Switch 2 hardware registered a big drop in sales during the first half of the current financial year (FY27).

Over that period, Nintendo sold 6.49m Switch 2 units and 1.27m units of the original Switch - equating to a 37.4 percent decline for Switch 2 and 32.7 percent decline for Switch 1 compared to the same period last year. Nintendo had previously forecast a decline in hardware sales, and the company still expects to sell 16.50m Switch 2 units by the end of the current fiscal year.

Nintendo software sales, on the other hand, saw a big year-on-year boost of 18.8 percent on Switch 2 (to 24.49m units) and a smaller increase of 6.8 percent on Switch 1. That's all thanks to the release of several popular first- and third-party titles over the first half of FY27. Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream was by far the most successful game with 8.81m units sold, followed by Rhythm Heaven Groove at 2.89m. Splatoon Raiders (the only Switch 2 exclusive of the three) sold 2.42m. Nintendo also highlighted a 60.5 percent year-on-year increase in digital game sales.
The increase in software unit sales and the "continued weakness of the Yen" couldn't prevent the overall business from declining by 15.3 percent year-on-year, however.

Other remaining releases in Nintendo' s current fiscal year include The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake (which launches today and was awarded five stars in Eurogamer's review), Switch 2 re-releases of Pikmin 2 and Xenoblade Chronicles 3, as well as Metroid Ravenous, which arrives early in 2027.

articles.headline: Ronaldo retires from Portugal duty
keyFacts: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from international football after a 23-year career with the Portugal national team.
The 41-year-old forward holds world records for scoring 146 goals and earning 234 caps for his country.
The Portuguese Football Federation plans to organize a tribute to honor Ronaldo for his contributions to the national team.
body: - Published
Portugal legend Cristiano Ronaldo says he is retiring from international football.
The 41-year-old forward has scored 146 goals and won 234 caps for his country - both world records - since making his debut in 2003.

His retirement comes after he walked out of the Portugal camp in September after being told he would not start the Nations League match against Denmark, resulting in a Â£215 fine from the Portuguese Football Federation (PFF).
"To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the number seven shirt of our national team," Ronaldo said in an Instagram video., external
"I never felt it belonged to me alone, but for 23 years I had the privilege and responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.
"Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision, because some decisions are not made with the mind alone - they are also made with the heart.
"A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end."
On Friday Portugal will announce their squad for this month's Nations League fixtures - against Denmark at home and Wales away.
The PFF said it not "let this farewell take place without due tribute".

A statement read: "It is our firm and immense desire to organise, plan, participate and actively collaborate in what will always be a fitting tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo's immense career, in which fans and the country can applaud and celebrate, once again, the player who has given us so much."
Ronaldo played in six European Championships. Portugal were runners-up in 2004 and won the competition in 2016.
The captain of his country since 2008, he also won the inaugural Nations League final in 2019 and repeated the feat in 2025.
However he was unable to lead his side beyond the quarter-finals at a World Cup, with a fourth place finish in 2006 his best showing at the tournament.
His great rival and Argentina legend Lionel Messi retired from international football on an emotional night in front of an 85,000-strong crowd in Buenos Aires in October.
Why did Ronaldo fall out with Portugal coach?
Ronaldo started every match in his sixth World Cup this summer, when Portugal lost to eventual champions Spain in the last 16.
His peformances in the tournament drew criticism in the media, with many observers questioning if he remained a force at international level.
He fell out with new coach Jorge Jesus after being named as a substitute against Norway.
Ronaldo was reportedly angry at being made to warm up in the second half but not brought on - the first time he was an unused substitute for Portugal in a competitive game since 2008.

When Jesus said in a news conference that Ronaldo would not start against Denmark, Ronaldo left the camp and issued a lengthy statement in which he said he would not be retiring and that Jesus had twice "broke his word".
Jesus said the door remained open for a return, while the PFF fined Ronaldo and suspended him for 30 days - a period that did not include any Portugal games.
Ronaldo did not directly reference the falling out in his farewell video, but did acknowledge that he had made mistakes.
"There were perfect afternoons and nights. There were victories I will never forget. There were defeats that still hurt to remember. I made mistakes, I suffered," said Ronaldo.
"There were also moments when I couldn't give the Portuguese people what they so desperately wanted. But I never gave up. And above all I never stopped feeling proud to represent Portugal.
"I spent my life working to become the best player in the world. Today, I realise my greatest victory was earning the honour of representing the best country in the world."

articles.headline: Iowa Democrat Eric Armstrong wins state House race despite dropping out in September
keyFacts: Democrat Eric Armstrong won the Iowa state House race for the 20th District despite withdrawing from the contest in September.
Armstrong withdrew from the race citing personal health issues but now intends to serve his constituents.
Republicans maintained their majorities in both the Iowa state House and state Senate despite the loss in this district.
body: An Iowa candidate came out on top in his race for state legislature Tuesday despite dropping out of the contest in September to address unspecified “personal health issues.”

Eric Armstrong, a retired railroad executive, was projected to defeat Republican Keith Jones by about nine percentage points in the Hawkeye State’s 20th House District, according to the Associated Press.

Armstrong announced he was quitting the race Sept. 7, saying in a statement on his campaign’s Facebook page: “Because I must prioritize my health and recovery at this time, I am stepping down from my campaign, effective immediately. This was a deeply difficult choice. However, I know it is the right one.

“Our District deserves a representative who can give 100 percent of their energy to this race. Right now, I must focus on healing so that I can continue to serve our community in other ways in the future.”
On Wednesday, Armstrong told the New York Times that he was “going to do my best” to represent his new constituents, but “I still have health issues, that’s what I’m struggling with.”
If able to take his seat in the Iowa House of Representatives, Armstrong will succeed fellow Democrat Josh Turek, who upset GOP Rep. Ashley Hinson to flip one of the state’s two US Senate seats.
In a small consolation, Iowa Republicans were able to hold onto their majorities in both the state House and state Senate with a handful of races left to be called as of Thursday morning.

articles.headline: Discord is ditching Electron and its new app uses less RAM
keyFacts: Discord is replacing the Electron framework with the Rust programming language for its desktop application.
Chief technology officer Stanislav Vishnevskiy stated the transition aims to improve performance and reduce memory usage.
Discord plans to begin user testing for the new Rust-based application soon.
body: Discord is finally giving up on Electron, the cross-platform framework that lets developers build desktop apps using web technologies. Electron web apps are notoriously heavy on system resources, and Discord is now moving its desktop app fully to Rust — a modern programming language designed for speed and memory safety.
Discord is ditching Electron and its new app uses less RAM
Discord is moving its apps fully over to the Rust programming language.

“We’ve been early adopters of Rust since 2018 and a lot of our infra, voice tech, and even some of the current client is already Rust, the holy grail was getting the whole client there,” explains Discord chief technology officer Stanislav Vishnevskiy in a post on X. “That means Electron goes away, and so does React Native, mobile keeps native UI but shares app code with desktop via Rust.”

Vishnevskiy also shared an image of the Discord Windows client using just 290MB of RAM, which is a clear improvement as you only have to participate in a few servers and RAM usage can easily hit 1GB or more using the current Windows app.
It’s not clear when Discord will make the full switch over to Rust, but Vishnevskiy says the company “hope to get it into testing with users soon.”

The update introduces a tiered V-Bucks system and removes monthly Crew Pack outfits.
The subscription price remains $11.99 while adding XP bonuses and access to multiple game passes.
body: Fortnite is set to completely overhaul its monthly subscription service, Fortnite Crew. Quite a few aspects of this feature are changing, so if you’re trying to figure out whether it’s still worth having, carefully reviewing all updated benefits is essential.

Whether you’re a longtime Fortnite Crew subscriber or someone who’s contemplating joining in, there’s a lot to consider with this overhaul. To ensure you fully understand what it entails, here are all Fortnite Crew overhaul changes explained, including a complete breakdown of everything it now offers.

And if you’re an ex-subscriber who chooses to rejoin between Dec. 6 and 31, your tier level will be treated specially, updating you to your most recent continuous subscription level from the past 12 months.
