articles.headline: An unexpected winner of the midterm election: Animals
keyFacts: Voters in Washington, DC, and Denver, Colorado, passed ballot measures to ban the sale of foie gras.
Colorado voters rejected a constitutional amendment that would have protected hunting and fishing methods currently banned in the state.
Two congressional candidates who opposed animal welfare laws lost their races, potentially shifting the legislative landscape for animal protection.
body: Olivia the duck — the mascot for the Washington, DC, campaign to ban foie gras — addresses a gaggle of reporters. | Zachariah Chou
In this week’s midterm elections , many Democrats won n a landslide. Also on the winning side of many ballot decisions: animals.

First, voters in Washington, DC, and Denver, Colorado, decisively supported a ban on the sale of foie gras — duck liver made by force-feeding the animals. In Colorado, voters opposed a constitutional amendment that would enshrine the right to hunt and fish, including with “traditional methods,” which could have allowed especially cruel (and currently illegal) practices, like poisoning and leg-hold traps.

And then there were the candidates. Two members of Congress who’ve led the charge on legislation to overturn farm animal welfare laws — Sen. Roger Marshall (R-KS) and Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-IA) — each lost their races. In Colorado, Manny Rutinel — a state lawmaker who’s championed animal welfare issues — defeated incumbent Republican Rep. Gabe Evans in the state’s Eighth Congressional District. One progressive candidate for agriculture secretary in Iowa, Chris Jones — who ran on promises to clean up livestock and farming pollution — did lose, although narrowly.

While neither political party has taken on animal welfare as a key issue on the stump or in their policy agendas, Democrats — though with some notable exceptions — are more likely to lead on animal welfare legislation and vote in favor of it. That means the blue tsunami that struck the US on Tuesday should ripple out to help advance animal welfare over the next two years.
The fight over foie gras is settled — for now
The campaign to ban foie gras won by huge margins, with support from 73 percent of DC voters and 66 percent of Denver voters .

Foie gras is made by force-feeding ducks via a metal pipe about 60 times in the final weeks before they’re killed. The practice causes their livers to swell to about six to 10 times their natural size, which is then turned into a thick spread that’s primarily consumed at high-end restaurants.

Foie gras farms and fine dining chefs contend that the practice is harmless, or at least not any worse than other factory farming practices. But veterinary research has concluded that it can in fact be quite painful for the birds.

“Tonight DC decided that force-feeding a bird has no place here,” Cady Witt of Pro-Animal DC — which put the measure on the ballot — said in a press release. “Thank you to everyone who signed the petition and voted to make DC a kinder place for animals.”

The DC and Denver votes follow foie gras sales bans in California, Pittsburgh, New York City, and Portland, Oregon. Over 20 European countries have banned the production of foie gras, and earlier this year, Brazil banned its sale and production. India banned the import of the product back in 2014.

But the foie gras fight in DC and Denver may just be getting started. A representative from Hudson Valley Farms, the largest US foie gras producer, told Axios last week that it’s considering legal challenges. Over the last week, Bart Hutchins — the head chef at Butterworth’s, a restaurant in Washington, DC — has held four-course foie gras tasting menu meals with proceeds going toward a potential legal challenge .
Coloradans rejected a “right to hunt and fish” constitutional amendment

Amendment 83 asked Colorado voters to enshrine “the right to hunt, fish, and harvest fish and wildlife by traditional methods” in the state’s constitution. Hunting and fishing are already protected by statute, and so “traditional method” is the key phrasing here.

“Read plainly, traditional methods could be interpreted to include practices like poisoning, leg hold traps, gill nets, or baiting and hounding,” Rebeecca Niemiec, co-director of Colorado State University’s Animal-Human Policy Center and a Colorado Parks and Wildlife commissioner , told Vox in October. These practices have been banned in Colorado, and Amendment 83 could’ve been a backdoor way to reverse those bans.

“Many of these practices injure or maim animals, including ones that aren’t targeted: Steel-jawed traps and poisons don’t discriminate between, say, a deer, a wolf, and a lynx,” my colleague Neel Dhanesha wrote in a story about wildlife issues on the ballot this election. The amendment would’ve also established hunting and fishing as the preferred means to manage fish and wildlife, over alternative — and more humane — methods, like birth control or animal relocation.

In other wildlife news, Massachusetts voters supported a ballot measure to fund nature conservation , while voters in Brevard County, Florida, supported the renewal of a tax that funds critical manatee and dolphin habitat restoration . Conservation measures in Arkansas and Rhode Island passed, too.
Two pro-factory farm politicians lost and a pro-animal welfare candidate won
In 2016, Massachusetts voters supported a ban on keeping egg-laying hens and pregnant pigs in small cages. Two years later, California voters supported a nearly identical law.

The laws don’t just ban confining these farmed animals in cages; they also prohibit restaurants and grocery stores from selling eggs and pork from animals kept in these cages no matter what state they were raised in. (Disclosure: I worked on the Massachusetts ballot measure.)

The pork industry has fought hard to overturn these laws, and two of its strongest congressional champions lost their races: Rep. Ashley Hinson (R-IA) and Sen. Roger Marshall (R-KS). Both have introduced several bills — most recently, the Save Our Bacon Act — that would overturn the state-level animal welfare laws. Pork producers and their Republican allies in Congress have worked to insert the legislation into the Farm Bill , but with Democrats soon to be in control of the House and Senate, their leverage has shrunk considerably.

Meanwhile, pro – animal welfare Colorado state lawmaker Manny Rutinel, a Democrat, defeated Republican incumbent Rep. Gabe Evans in a competitive race for the state’s Eighth District. Prior to running for office, Rutinel was an attorney at the nonprofit Earthjustice, where he sued meat companies for pollution. The state’s Eighth District also happens to be home to massive industrial agricultural operations, including one of the largest meat packing plants in the country.

But one agriculture reformer did lose a race. Chris Jones, a former Big Ag insider turned vocal critic , lost his race to become Iowa’s next agriculture secretary. Jones, a water quality expert, centered his campaign on the poor state of Iowa’s waterways, which have been heavily polluted by the state’s massive hog, egg, and ethanol industries, and could be linked to rising cancer rates in Iowa .

Animals get little direct attention in politics, but each election has massive consequences for them, including the billions of animals confined in factory farms across the US and countless wildlife caught in rivers and hunted for sport. This election was evidence that, when given the opportunity, voters want to help animals. And with a Democratic majority headed to Congress, there may be even more opportunities to advance animal welfare in 2027.

articles.headline: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Changes to the Infamous Water Temple Are Actually Brilliant
keyFacts: The new Ocarina of Time remake for Switch 2 includes updates to make the infamous Water Temple dungeon easier to navigate.
Director Eiji Aonuma requested these adjustments to address the dungeon's long-standing reputation for being difficult to complete.
New features include clearer visual signposting for water controls, color-coded pipes, and improved item management to reduce menu pausing.
body: With The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Switch 2 remake out now, long-time Nintendo fans are in for a lot of warm nostalgia. A trek through the lost woods, duets with Sheik, a return to the Bombchu Bowling Alley — all of those wonderful moments return in a faithful remake that feels every bit as magical as the Nintendo 64 classic. But with all those wonderful moments comes a painful reunion with one of the most hated moments in Zelda history. Yes, you will have to return to the dreaded Water Temple.

Don’t worry! Even though the Ocarina of Time remake is careful not to change too much about the original game, it does make some small tweaks to a dungeon that still haunts a generation. It’s mercifully easier to navigate now thanks to a few minor but smart updates that go a long way.

The Water Temple is the most infamous dungeon in the original Ocarina of Time, so much so that it has been a bit of a running joke for decades now. The gist is that it’s a four-story structure built around a central room, and it’s flooded with water. To access certain areas, you need to find rooms in the dungeon that allow you to change the water level throughout the temple. Easy enough on paper, but it’s a bit of a pain in practice. Due to the limited visual information you get in-game, it requires you to keep a mental map of where each water adjustment point is, as well as how each of the three levels will change the layout of the dungeon. It’s a headache to keep everything straight, thus earning it a reputation as a frustrating rite of passage.

While that structure hasn’t changed much in the remake, Nintendo does make it easier to get through with a few smart decisions. That came at the request of Eiji Aonuma, who directed the original Ocarina of Time. “I had some overdue homework: I wanted to do something about the Water Temple I created 28 years ago,” Aonuma said in a recent Nintendo developer interview. “Since it became well known for its difficulty in the original game, I had the team make some adjustments in this version.”

One of those adjustments just comes down to clearer signposting. Building off the dungeon’s Ocarina of Time 3D redesign, the doors that lead to water controls are now clearly marked with symbols showing you exactly how the water level will change. You no longer have to remember which door leads to the room that drains the room, or which one will get you to floor two.

On top of that, each of the routes are now color-coded. You’ll find variously colored pipes around each of the three doors, and those visually lead you to the control room if you follow them through the dungeon. For instance, when you enter the route to the room that brings the water to its lowest level, you’ll notice that some blue pipes signal that you should float to the water’s surface. Follow that hint and you’ll find that the pipes lead to clearly marked pedestals for you to play your ocarina on. All of that makes it significantly easier to remember exactly where you need to go at all times.

Arguably, the more impactful Water Temple change comes from a top-level control decision that just so happens to make life easier in the dungeon. Part of why the Water Temple is such a pain is because you need to use a few key items throughout it. Your ocarina, Iron Boots, Hookshot, and more all play major roles in solving puzzles throughout the temple. Since the original game only gave you three item slots to work with, you were often left juggling around your item shortcuts in the main menu. It’s a minor pain point, but one that stands out when you’re constantly swapping items.

While the Switch 2 remake still has its own item management quirks, it wisely keeps your ocarina mapped to the D-pad at all times. Your boots get a quick swap button on the down button there too, meaning that you don’t need to waste an item slot on the Iron Boots. With those two necessities free up, you can dedicate your ZR item slot to the Hookshot and only swap to other items as needed with a quick menu on the R button. That decision cuts out any need for pause-menu management, allowing you to move through the dungeon more fluidly.

For the ‘90s purists, these changes might sound a little sacrilegious. As much as players claim to hate the Water Temple, that complaint invariably comes with a fondness for a genuinely memorable bit of frustrating design. “Why shouldn’t today’s youths struggle through the Water Temple like their elders once did?” you may ask. I, for one, welcome the help, just as I support the idea of today’s students having their loans canceled even though I had to pay mine off. The new visual design tweak makes for some sensible signposting that still feels part of the dungeon’s architecture, and the control solution just makes it easier to stay immersed in a well-built dungeon. New generations of players needn’t suffer like us old Zelda fans once did. Swim free, ye tadpoles.

articles.headline: White House official details what gets Trump’s attention in intelligence briefings
keyFacts: A White House official stated that President Trump often focuses on individual crime victims during intelligence briefings despite his interest in large-scale cartel operations.
The administration is using the Homeland Security Task Force to coordinate over 20 federal agencies to dismantle entire criminal organizations rather than just arresting leaders.
The task force aims to reduce the ability of criminal networks to threaten Americans by targeting transportation, distribution, and money laundering operations nationwide.
body: EXCLUSIVE: President Donald Trump may be briefed on sprawling cartel networks and massive drug seizures, but sometimes it's the story of a single American crime victim that captures his attention, a White House official told Fox News Digital.

The official described how Trump can shift from discussions about major criminal organizations to an individual harmed by crime, pressing officials about what more the federal government can do to protect everyday Americans.
"I could be talking about very grand cartel stuff, which he's very interested in," the official said, explaining that the president may instead focus on one person hurt by criminal activity.
WHITE HOUSE HIGHLIGHTS 'STEEPEST' EVER DECLINE IN US CASUALTIES FROM CARTELS AMID BOAT STRIKES

The official said Trump receives regular briefings that include photographs of narcotics seized by federal agents. While the president takes pride in successful enforcement operations, the official described his reaction as quickly turning to the amount of work still ahead.

The president's response to the photographs, according to the official, is to ask what more can be done to stop the flow of drugs into American communities. Trump also pressed for federal agencies to work together as the administration seeks to dismantle entire criminal organizations rather than simply arrest their leaders as agencies have done in the past.
That approach is at the center of a campaign that has brought together more than 20 federal agencies under the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF) initiative.

According to figures provided by the White House, the task forces made nearly 12,000 arrests during fiscal year 2026, seized approximately 161 metric tons of drugs, $482 million in criminal assets and nearly 13,000 weapons.
ICE ARRESTS MORE THAN 100 ALLEGED GANG MEMBERS IN SINGLE WEEK, INCLUDING VIOLENT MS-13, TDA SUSPECTS: DHS

The administration also reported 676 criminal organizations disrupted in figures provided to Fox News Digital. The task forces have 6,585 active investigations, including more than 1,000 targeting major drug kingpins and 814 targeting designated Foreign Terrorist Organizations.

The task force operates nationwide, bringing together federal law enforcement agencies with hundreds of state, local and international partners. Its public website, HSTF.gov , outlines the initiative's mission, participating agencies and enforcement efforts targeting cartels, transnational gangs and other criminal organizations.

Behind those numbers, the official described an effort to break down longstanding divisions among federal law enforcement agencies that previously pursued overlapping investigations with varying degrees of cooperation.
DOJ TOUTS HUNDREDS OF GUN, DRUG ARRESTS AS ST LOUIS SURGE OPERATION ENDS: 'VIOLENCE IS NOT INEVITABLE'
The official said more than 1,800 cartel-related narcotics task forces previously operated across the country, with varying degrees of coordination.
Agencies including the FBI , DEA and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) could pursue overlapping targets, occasionally competing to bring indictments first.
Interagency disagreements sometimes left investigations stalled for years, the official said.

Under the new approach, the National Coordination Center brings together the Departments of Justice and Homeland Security, with support from military and intelligence partners, to resolve conflicts and coordinate investigations across jurisdictions.
DRUG CARTEL KINGPIN AMONG TARGETS IN SWEEPING TRUMP CRACKDOWN ON ALLEGED MEXICAN CORRUPTION NETWORK
"Now we're all indicting together," the official said.
Rather than focusing exclusively on high-value targets, investigators are pursuing the transportation networks, distributors, collectors and money launderers that keep criminal enterprises operating.
The official explained that taking down a cartel leader does not necessarily dismantle the organization because others can quickly assume leadership.
"There's five more people ready to step up as soon as we take out one," the official said.
A sweeping federal investigation into the Trinitarios gang in Massachusetts illustrates the kind of coordinated law enforcement effort the administration is pursuing.
In June, federal prosecutors announced racketeering conspiracy charges against 26 alleged gang leaders, members and associates in connection with five murders and 19 attempted murders.

The announcement brought the total number of Trinitarios members charged in related investigations over two years to 56. Prosecutors alleged the gang's involvement in 11 murders and 30 attempted murders since 2017.

Court documents describe chapters operating in the Boston area whose members allegedly engaged in drug trafficking, kidnappings and witness intimidation. Investigators also alleged the gang recruited minors attending local schools, sometimes using younger members to conceal weapons or serve as lookouts.

The investigation involved HSI, the FBI, DEA, ATF and state and local law enforcement partners. The investigation began before the HSTF initiative, and the charges remain allegations against defendants who have not been convicted.
The task force's reach also extends to drug trafficking operations moving narcotics across state lines.
In Louisiana, federal prosecutors announced five cases involving more than a dozen defendants and hundreds of kilograms of narcotics.

Near Breaux Bridge, investigators discovered approximately 147 kilograms of methamphetamine concealed inside modified ice cream freezers. In another case near Lafayette, authorities found approximately 100 kilograms of cocaine hidden inside an 18-wheeler's cab.

The White House official also pointed to Tren de Aragua, the Venezuelan criminal organization that drew national attention during the 2024 presidential campaign, as an example of the administration's broader strategy.

Fox News Digital extensively covered allegations of Tren de Aragua activity at apartment complexes in Aurora, Colorado, including accounts from local officials and residents who described violence and intimidation.
Trump subsequently made Aurora a recurring focus of his criticism of the Biden administration's border policies.

The official recalled Fox News Digital's reporting on the controversy and argued that the administration's coordinated enforcement campaign has weakened the gang's ability to operate openly in the United States.
"I'm not saying they're completely gone here, but they are so on their heels because we have this concerted effort taken," the official said.
"You don't see them bragging in the social media anymore," the official added.

In May, the Justice Department announced charges against more than 25 defendants in a nationwide Tren de Aragua crackdown spanning six federal judicial districts. Authorities reported seizing more than 80 firearms, approximately 18 kilograms of narcotics and more than $100,000.
The official described the crackdown as an example of the administration's effort to pursue criminal organizations at multiple levels, rather than concentrating solely on their leaders.
The administration is seeking to apply that same approach to more deeply established criminal networks, including the notorious Sinaloa Cartel .
The official said the task force's ultimate objective is not simply accumulating arrests or celebrating drug seizures, but reducing the ability of criminal organizations to threaten Americans.

For Trump, the official said, even major seizures can serve as reminders of the work still ahead. The president may take pride in enforcement results, but the official described his attention as quickly turning to how much more needs to be done to stop narcotics from reaching American communities.

articles.headline: Amazon teams with Uber Eats for new Prime perks
keyFacts: Amazon Prime members can now place Uber Eats orders directly through the Amazon website and shopping app in the United States.
Prime members receive zero delivery fees on Uber Eats orders of at least $25 placed through Amazon platforms.
Amazon stated the integration could save Prime users up to $175 annually depending on their delivery usage.
body: Amazon teams with Uber Eats for new Prime perks
Order on Amazon’s platforms and (sometimes) skip the delivery fees.

Amazon has a pretty long list of perks for members of its Prime subscription program, and today brings a new addition. The company now supports placing Uber Eats orders directly on its Amazon.com website and in the Amazon Shopping app in the US. The partnership with Uber will also grant $0 delivery fees to Prime Members on their Uber Eats orders of $25 or more placed via Amazon, as well as a promise of "Prime-exclusive offers available only on Amazon." No separate Uber account is needed to place the delivery orders and nearly 10,000 cities and towns in the US will support the integration.

According to the release from Amazon, the Uber Eats integration could save Prime users as much as $175 a year, although the exact amount will obviously vary depending on how much you rely on delivery for meals.

Amazon offered a year of free GrubHub+ access along with Prime starting in 2022. This subscription program, which includes $0 delivery fees and other perks tied to GrubHub orders, became a permanent benefit of Prime in 2024.

articles.headline: "BioWare's closure represents an immense loss to and possibly a targeted attack on Canada's cultural legacy" argues petition calling on Canadian government to step in
keyFacts: A petition calling for the Canadian government to resurrect the shuttered studio BioWare has reached the 500-signature threshold for an official response.
The petition argues that BioWare's closure is a loss to Canada's cultural legacy and requests government capital to make the studio independent from Electronic Arts.
The petition will now be presented to the Canadian House of Commons, where the government is required to provide an official response.
body: Calls for the Canadian government to help ressurect recently shuttered RPG makers BioWare have progressed from a single post by a politician to a petition with enough signatures that it looks set to be presented to the Canadian House of Commons for an official response. So far, 1,662 people from the country of maple syrup and also other things have signed this call for their leaders to consider stepping in.

"BioWare is one of Canada's most important cultural exports to the world in the 21st century, selling tens of millions of units of their video games globally," declares the petition, started by Brendan Routh and authorised by Vancouver Kingsway MP Don Davies.

"BioWare's productions champion the values of inclusivity, tolerance, democracy, justice, and civil rights that are at the centre of Canada's national identity," its run of bullet points continues. "BioWare has been shuttered by its American parent company Electronic Arts, now owned by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Jared Kushner's Affinity Partners and BioWare's closure represents an immense loss to and possibly a targeted attack on Canada's cultural legacy."

With all of that in mind, the petition calls on the Canadian Government to "provide BioWare with the capital necessary to secure independence of themselves and their intellectual property from Electronic Arts and resume business as an independent, Canadian company". The Canadians who've signed also want their leaders to "protect Canadian businesses and cultural institutions from being dictated by American and foreign corporate interests" and "champion the values of inclusivity, tolerance, democracy, justice, and civil rights at the centre of Canada's national identity by preserving BioWare's invaluable contribution to the global entertainment industry".

Thus far, the petition's amassed 1,662 verified signatures from citizens across Canada, putting it above the 500 verified signature threshold required for it to be presented to the country's House of Commons. That'll be followed by the tabling of an official response from the Canadian government.

As with some of the responses from political bodies the likes of the Stop Killing Games campaign have gotten over the years, I find it hard not to see this petition not being greeted with an answer along the lines of 'We do care about this and thank you for raising it, but we're not really gonna do much here'. I think a full BioWare resurrection with government backing is highly unlikely, but finding some way to enshrine the studio's legacy or contribution to Canada's games industry and arts culture seems a lot more easily doable.

A big statue of Blokeshep and Femshep surrounded by their crew of potential allies somewhere in Edmonton, maybe. Or a big stone middle finger that's always required to be aimed at a poster for the next Star Wars film/game/TV show/bit of merch.

- "Mass Effect was my ultimate white whale": Journey composer shares 20 minutes of music created during talks to work on BioWare's recently cancelled RPG

articles.headline: Cristiano Ronaldo calls time on Portugal career after 234 caps and 146 goals
keyFacts: Cristiano Ronaldo announced his retirement from the Portugal national team after a 23-year career spanning 234 caps and 146 goals.
Ronaldo left the national team training camp following a disagreement with coach Jorge Jesus regarding his playing time.
The Portuguese Football Federation plans to organize a tribute to honor Ronaldo for his contributions to the national team.
body: Cristiano Ronaldo has announced that he will not play for Portugal any more, ending an international career that spanned six World Cups and included a European title and the men’s all-time scoring record.

The announcement marked the end of a lauded career that began more than two decades ago before Euro 2004 and finished with him walking out on the national team after falling out with coach Jorge Jesus.

“To the Portuguese people, the day has come for me to hand back the No 7 shirt of our national team,” the 41-year-old Ronaldo said in a long video message on social media. “I never felt it belonged to me alone but for 23 years I had the privilege and the responsibility of wearing it, defending it and carrying it with me into stadiums all around the world.

“Today the time has come to pass it on to the future. It was not an easy decision because some decisions are not made with the mind alone. They are also made with the heart. A journey that began in August 2003 and changed my life forever has come to an end.”

While long-time peer Lionel Messi finished his career with Argentina after a much-anticipated farewell match last month, Ronaldo’s final appearance with Portugal has ended up being on 24 September in a 1-0 win over Wales in the Nations League. Jesus kept him on the bench for the following match and said he didn’t plan to start him in the next one, so Ronaldo decided to leave the team’s training camp. Jesus later said Ronaldo would be welcome back and the decision to return was up to him.

The Portuguese Football Federation released a statement expressing “deep gratitude and immense admiration” for Ronaldo’s service to the country, which began with a first international appearance in August 2003. “Cristiano Ronaldo has raised Portugal’s profile and inspired generations of young people who dream of following in his footsteps; for many of us, he is the greatest player of all time!” the federation said. It said it intends to organise a tribute to Ronaldo “in which the fans and the country can one more time applaud and celebrate a player who has given us so much”.

Like Messi, Ronaldo will keep playing at club level, and is expected to finish his club career at the end of this season with Al-Nassr in Saudi Arabia. He is in pursuit of his 1,000th career goal and sits on 985. Of those, a record 146 goals came in 234 appearances with Portugal.

articles.headline: Safer Water at Home: New Water Heater Tech Aims to Kill Bacteria in the Tank
keyFacts: Researchers at the National Institute of Standards and Technology patented a water heater design that kills Legionella bacteria by maintaining 160-degree tank temperatures.
The design uses an unmixed heat exchanger to cool water to safe levels for human use before it leaves the tank.
The technology's availability to consumers depends on when manufacturers license the patent and develop products for the home market.
body: One challenge of current water heater designs is staying hot enough to kill harmful bacteria like Legionella pneumophila, which can cause Legionnaires’ disease. A new water heater design, developed and patented by researchers at the National Institute of Standards and Technology, aims to raise tank temperatures to 160 degrees Fahrenheit, which spells instant doom for Legionella bacteria.

Legionella bacteria love warm water, so while they struggle to survive in a water heater tank set to 120 F, they’re more than comfortable elsewhere in a home’s hot water pipes. It’s technically possible to achieve sufficient temperatures with existing water heaters, but those temperatures are also likely to scald human skin whenever you turn on the faucet.

The biggest innovation of this new design is how it finds a new use for heat exchangers, the same technology behind air conditioners, heat pumps, furnaces and refrigerators. I wanted to know more, so I reached out to David Yashar, a NIST mechanical engineer behind the new design.
More from CNET
How this new water heater design works

As Yashar and his team researched ways to kill Legionella bacteria, they needed to figure out how to make tank temperatures around 160 F safe and practical for humans. They ultimately landed on the concept of using cold water entering the water heater to cool the hot water leaving the tank with an unmixed heat exchanger that contains the water inlet and outlet.

The principle behind unmixed heat exchangers—where the fluids don’t mix—is that incoming cold water gets a heating boost from the hot-water outlet while cooling the water to safe levels for people. As a result, the tank can maintain the high temperatures required to prevent pathogen growth behind illnesses like Legionnaires’ disease, which has a fatality rate of around 10%, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Beyond the safety benefits, the process recaptures some waste heat and can improve heating efficiency for the cold water, since it enters the tank warmer.
Inspired by HVAC tech

I’ve covered various heating, ventilation and air conditioning tech over the years, so I immediately recognized similarities between the new design’s unmixed heat exchanger and those used in HVAC and refrigerators. For example, air conditioners use a heat exchanger for the refrigeration cycle (also called the Carnot cycle) to pull heat from air inside your home (evaporator coil) and push it outside (condenser coil) without pulling in outside air. Additionally, heat pumps may use a heat exchanger for defrosting ice buildup when in heating mode.

When I asked about the similarities, Yashar noted that it wasn’t a coincidence that his patent took inspiration from HVAC and refrigeration tech. Yashar said, “My background is in HVAC&R, and it is very common to use unmixed heat exchangers like this to manipulate the bounds of the Carnot cycle to achieve some specific condition. I came up with the idea when I first learned about Legionella and the existing mitigation strategies.” He goes on to explain that using an unmixed heat exchanger “across the inlet and outlet was a very simple, effective, and inexpensive way to push the water temperature up to that condition and back down.”

It’s fitting that Yashar discovered better ways for heat exchangers not only to kill pathogens, but also to improve energy efficiency. Finding new applications for existing technology is certainly an underrated aspect of invention.
When can consumers buy this new type of water heater?

As exciting as this tech is, a patent doesn’t necessarily mean it will hit the market immediately. Yashar notes that while his research “proved the concept using a 60-gallon tank,” it depends on when manufacturers license the technology and get their engineers working on designing consumer products suitable for homes. This process could happen quickly or take several years.

Because Yashar’s concept essentially modified an existing water heater, I asked if it would be possible to retrofit products in people’s homes. He notes that NIST’s project started with the intention of modifying the tank’s hardware and controls. “The steps we took might not be simple tasks for an existing application,” said Yashar. “It really depends on a lot of things, so it is best if people learn how this works and understand how to achieve it within their existing application.”

He brings up one important consideration: Retrofit tanks will need extra insulation to be worth it. It’s “absolutely necessary for a retrofit because the tank temperature will be about 40 degrees hotter than what the existing system was designed for. If this isn’t done, the standby losses would be very large.” Without appropriate insulation, any efficiency gained by the heat exchanger would be lost to heat loss in standby mode.
So, while a retrofit might be possible, it seems more likely to engineer a product from the ground up based on this design, especially if consumers want to keep utility costs manageable.
For more tips, see the best temperature to set your thermostat this winter and learn how to find air leaks in your home for more efficient heating.

articles.headline: Nintendo Rules Out Further Switch 2 Price Rises as Console Sales and Profit Fall
keyFacts: Nintendo reported a 16% drop in operating profit and a 41% decline in Switch 2 console sales for the recent quarter.
President Shuntaro Furukawa stated that Nintendo will not increase the price of the Switch 2 further despite current financial challenges.
Investors hope the new Ocarina of Time remake will boost holiday sales after concerns regarding a lack of high-profile game titles.
body: Nintendo has ruled out further Switch 2 price rises while reporting falling console sales and reduced profit.

According to Bloomberg , operating profit fell 16% to 73.9 billion ‌yen (approx. $467 million) during the three months to September 30, off the back of a 15% decline in sales. CNBC said Nintendo sold 2.67 million Switch 2 units in the quarter, down 41% from the same period last year and down from the 3.82 million units that were sold during the first quarter of the current financial year (April to June 2026). Nintendo raised the price of Switch 2 in September, fueled by the ongoing ‘RAMpocalypse’ that has also seen Microsoft and Sony raise the price of their consoles.

Despite this, Reuters reported that Nintendo President Shuntaro Furukawa insisted Nintendo had enough memory to meet its forecasted Switch 2 sales of 16.5 million units for the financial year ending March 2027, and is not considering further price changes.

Nintendo launches the Ocarina of Time remake today, and investors are hoping it will boost sales of the Switch 2 during the holiday sales season. Reuters said that investors remain concerned that the memory situation, as well as a “lack of high-profile titles” for Switch 2 this year, could negatively affect the console's momentum.

Nintendo's financial report reveals data for the first half of the current financial year, (from April to September 2026). During that six month period, Nintendo sold 6.49 million Switch 2 units, down from the 10.36 million it sold during the same period last year.

But there's important context to note here. Lifetime sales of the Switch 2 are now 26.35 million, which means it’s still outpacing the original Switch in terms of launch aligned sales (the first six quarters after release). It’s also worth noting that the Switch 2 enjoyed a record-breaking launch, fueled by ample stock availability, that saw it become the fastest-selling console of all time , so it was always going to be up against tough comparisons during its second year.
And countering apparent concern from investors, shares in Nintendo jumped 8.13% today following the release of the Ocarina of Time remake and the company's financial report.

As for video game sales, Tomodachi Life: Living the Dream sold 8.81 million units, Rhythm Heaven Groove sold 2.89 million units, and Splatoon Raiders sold 2.42 million units. Mario Kart World, which launched alongside the Switch 2 last year, “continued to sell steadily,” Nintendo said, shifting a further 1.78 million units during the two quarters.

Elsewhere, StarFox, released in June, sold 1.17 million units, and Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave, released in September, sold 1.34 million units. The expectation is that Nintendo will have some big hitters for Switch 2 in 2027, including, fans hope, the next mainline Super Mario game. Pokémon Winds & Pokémon Waves are confirmed for next year.

“Nintendo’s only real blockbuster this fiscal year is the Ocarina Of Time remake," Serkan Toto, CEO of Kantan Games, told CNBC . "It’s not enough to make investors happy, especially after the device is now as expensive as it is.

“It’s getting harder and harder to sell video game hardware these days, and only hits help. Nintendo must step on the gas and deliver more big games next fiscal year to make sure the Switch 2 momentum continues.”

articles.headline: SAP promises to open out data flows in both directions
keyFacts: SAP is adopting native support for the Apache Iceberg open table format to enable bidirectional data sharing across enterprise systems.
The company expanded its partnership with Databricks to allow users to integrate legacy ERP data into modern cloud analytics platforms for AI development.
SAP plans to integrate its Joule AI assistant with Databricks' Genie platform to facilitate automated actions using shared enterprise data.
body: SAP has taken meaningful steps in opening its data to bidrectional sharing across the enteprise, and in decoupling the advanced analytics needed for AI from its ERP upgrade path.

During a technical conference last week, the German software giant adopted native support for Apache Iceberg, the open table format, and extended its partnership with Databricks to bring data from legacy ERP systems into its modern cloud analytics platform.

"By putting [a] stake in the ground with Iceberg, we now have SAP moving from a very closed application storage model to an open lakehouse model," said Aaron Rosenbaum, Gartner senior director analyst, referring to the concept which brings together data lakes and warehouses.

Also important was the bridge between modern analytics in the cloud and on-prem or hosted legacy systems such as ECC, the ERP system broadly adopted by global companies. "SAP made a pretty big move in saying we're going to open this up, not just to S/4HANA Cloud [the latest ERP system], but ECC users. That coupling — leveraging of AI, leveraging a lakehouse for AI to the ERP upgrade lifecycle — was a problem," said Rosenbaum.

In May this year, SAP bought Dremio, a lakehouse platform built around Apache Iceberg, ending its previous preference for Databricks' Delta Sharing to bring together SAP data products with existing lakehouses bi-directionally.

At SAP's TedEd conference last week, SAP said its Business Data Cloud (BDC) – the "trusted data foundation for SAP Business AI Platform" – would now support native Apache Iceberg and a universal catalog powered by Apache Polaris, "providing an open and governed data foundation for users and [AI agent platform] Joule to consume data."

Together with SAP BDC Connect, the new tech policy will support platform interoperability with "zero-copy data sharing" across platforms from Databricks, Snowflake, Google, AWS, and Microsoft. The system would also continue to support Delta Lake, the alternative open table format from Databricks, SAP said .
With the integration of Dremio's SQL query engine, BDC users will also get access to relational databases including SQL Server, MongoDB, Oracle, and PostgreSQL without moving data, the vendor said.

During the same conference, Databricks – the lakehouse company born out of an Apache Spark platform – extended its partnership with SAP based on the previously announced SAP Databricks, which embeds the Databricks Data + AI Platform in BDC.

That "expanded scope" promises to make data from SAP applications available for consumption in the SAP Business Data Cloud engine of choice, including SAP Databricks. The vendor said that a manufacturer running finance and supply chain on SAP ECC on-premises, for example, could use SAP Application Data Foundation to bring historic order data into SAP Databricks, combining it with third-party data, and allowing data engineers to build demand-forecasting models on SAP's business semantics, without custom extraction pipelines. They can keep that work as they move to the cloud, Databricks suggested .

This being 2026, the hoped-for output from all of this data engineering is not just business insight, but automated action, by way of AI agents. SAP has its Joule AI assistant and agentic platform, while Databricks has Genie , and the two companies have promised to bring them together.

The increasing openness is good for users who will get more options in plotting a strategy to bring together enterprise data, leaving them pondering over where to put the business context layer, which vendors will no doubt fight to control, Rosenbaum said.

"You have the comment that they're going to bring Joule and Genie together in the future. This is pointing to a struggle that's going on throughout enterprises and throughout all the vendors about the context layer. I don't necessarily see that there's one winner. You do have different points of context within the transaction system and across the whole business, and they have been points of tension.
"Lack of single vendor lock-in is important. It's something that all the customers are struggling with: how do we build these context layers and deliver sort of consistent answers?"

SAP's shift in the direction of openness is likely to help users in this struggle, whether they choose to build the context layer within the ERP vendor's data platform using its semantic layer, or outside of it using tools from other vendors – there are plenty of companies offering help for those opening their wallets.
Nonetheless, whichever path users choose, a lot of work lies ahead. ®

articles.headline: Series of bomb threats cause flight disruptions across Europe
keyFacts: A wave of anonymous bomb threats caused widespread flight diversions and security operations across Europe on Thursday.
Authorities confirmed that no explosives were found on any of the targeted flights after security teams conducted inspections.
Officials have not identified the source of the threats or received any claims of responsibility for the disruptions.
body: LONDON — A wave of bomb threats caused chaos in the skies and airports of Europe on Thursday, the latest in a series of incidents that have prompted emergency landings and security sweeps on runways this week.
No explosives have so far been found, and it is not clear who or what is behind the calls. But the threats alone have caused disruption to Europe’s airspace and some of its busiest airports.

One of the first reports involved Aer Lingus flight EI402 from Dublin to Rome, which changed course near Paris and diverted to a French Air Force base, the airline said. There, all 151 passengers and six crew were evacuated from the plane while the bomb squad inspected the aircraft, French Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu’s office said in a statement.
Confirmed flights threatened Thursday
- Aer Lingus EI402 from Dublin to Rome — received bomb threat over France, made emergency landing at air base and inspected by bomb squad, according to airline and French officials.
- AY1761 Finnair from Helsinki to Rome Fiumicino — escorted into Rome by Italian Air Force jets, bomb-squad search found no explosives, airline said.
- AY1471 Finnair from Helsinki to Vienna — also received bomb threat, likewise no explosives found, according to airline.
- LO235 LOT Polish Airlines from Warsaw to Brussels — crew made midair checks after receiving threat, "additional screening" once in Brussels found no "suspicious items," airline said.
- LO331 Polish Airlines from Warsaw to Paris — "affected by a potential threat" but searches of passengers and luggage found nothing, Polish officials said.
- FR3606 Ryanair flight from Copenhagen to Sofia...
- ...and FR6410 Ryanair flight from Madrid to Sofia — both landed normally following bomb threat, no explosives found, according to Bulgarian transport ministry.
- FR1730 Ryanair flight from London Stansted to Sofia — also received a bomb threat and diverted to Plovdiv, the transport ministry said.
- WMT3064 Wizz Air from Milan to Bucharest — airport said it was notified of the bomb threat as flight was arriving, bomb squad found nothing.
- Czech police say four unidentified flights headed for Prague have also received threats.
From there, reports of threats in the skies over Europe arrived at dizzying pace, triggering searches by cabin crews and then again by airport security once on the ground.
Security operations were launched at airports in Prague, Copenhagen and Warsaw, with passengers at the last seeing the military and police sniffer dogs patrolling the tarmac.

A Finnair flight from Helsinki was escorted by Italian Air Force jets to Rome’s Fiumicino Airport “following anonymous reports of a suspected bomb threat,” according to a spokesperson for the city’s airport authority. Bomb disposal experts found nothing.

“Unfortunately, air traffic is sometimes subject to threats, as we have seen this week, when other airlines in Europe have also faced hoax bomb threats,” a Finnair spokesperson, Stiina Tuunanen, told NBC News in an email. “Threats are almost always unfounded.”
That was also the case for another Finnair flight from Helsinki to Vienna, whose threat was found to be baseless after landing safely in the Austrian capital.
LOT Polish Airlines said two of its aircraft from Warsaw were targeted, one flying to Brussels and the other to Paris.

Back on the ground in Warsaw, Polish resident Matthew Bojarsky, 28, was about to fly to Paris for a romantic trip with his American girlfriend, but saw police, military and sniffer dogs on the tarmac, he told NBC News. Passengers were told that “safety protocols” meant their flight, LOT LO331, had to be aborted and moved to a later time.

Elsewhere, three Ryanair flights were interrupted as they headed to the Bulgarian capital Sofia. Two flights, from Copenhagen and Milan, landed at their destination, while a third, from London, was diverted to the Bulgarian city of Plovdiv, the country’s transport ministry said in an email.
Ryanair did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
In the Czech Republic, meanwhile, police said they had received threats about improvised explosive devices being place on four planes heading to the country’s capital Prague.

Thursday’s incidents follow days of airline bomb threats that have forced multiple flights to divert and an airport in Poland to briefly close. No explosive devices were found in the earlier incidents, according to authorities in various countries.

On Tuesday, a security operation was also launched at the Greek island port of Syros after a bomb threat to an Israel-bound cruise ship. Authorities said an unknown person claimed an explosive device had been attached to the hull of the Panama-flagged Crown Iris that was due to sail to Haifa.
Authorities have not indicated who could have been behind the incidents and there were no claims of responsibility.

articles.headline: Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe first drive: Where tech and fun collide
keyFacts: The Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe is the first battery-powered vehicle developed exclusively by the AMG division.
Mercedes utilizes the AMG.EA architecture and axial flux motors to manage battery weight and improve vehicle handling.
The AMG GT 63 model features three motors that produce up to 1,153 peak horsepower.
body: The night before I drove the AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, I complained to a group of journalists that automakers don’t want to take chances and just build fun, weird cars anymore. About 12 hours later, Mercedes made me eat my words. Outside of all the bombastic extravaganza of the Los Angeles launch, the first true AMG powered exclusively by batteries is a technological triumph that’s as comfortable on the track as it is on the street. And it’s really very good on the track.
Triforce

One of the fundamental problems with EVs is weight. Batteries are heavy, and the old rule about an object in motion tending to stay in motion makes the notion of nimble cornering a difficult engineering problem. Mercedes loves an engineering problem, and after two days behind the wheel of the AMG GT EV, the company has mostly reduced the battery-weight tax that mires EV performance.

On the road and on the track, the vehicle is firmly planted to the roadway. Mercedes says various technologies make this possible. In addition to decades of producing high-performance vehicles, the automaker’s AMG.EA sports-car architecture does a lot of heavy lifting here, constantly adjusting power delivery from the three motors while guiding the Active Ride Control suspension, steering—including up to six degrees at the rear axle—and active aerodynamics to deliver the performance AMG customers have come to expect from a vehicle with the Affalterbach badge on the hood.

Of the technology added to the vehicle, the axial flux motors are the most intriguing. Three motors offer a lighter, smaller powertrain that unlocks a host of abilities: two that are 3.1 inches (79 mm) wide in the back, one that’s 3.5 inches (89 mm) wide in the front. Produced by Yasa, which Mercedes bought in 2021, the motors output up to 1,153 hp (860 kW) of peak power in the AMG GT 63, with a nominal output of 711 hp (530 kW) and 1,475 lb-ft (2,000 Nm). During Boost mode, the additional horsepower is available for 63 seconds. Because it’s the AMG GT 63, obviously.

articles.headline: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time’s NPCs Stay Busy All Night, And Sounds Like That Was A Pain
keyFacts: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 features a new 24-hour routine for all NPCs in Hyrule Castle Town.
Producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi stated that creating these full-day schedules required significant extra work and daily dialogue reviews.
Fujibayashi supported the change to encourage younger staff members to implement new ideas and modernize the game experience.
body: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 is a mostly faithful remake, but it does introduce some new features and bells and whistles that modernize the experience. Some of those are very noticeable, like the addition of a jump button, while others are more subtle. One such subtle change is the new full-day passage of time inside Hyrule Castle Town, which also means NPCs need something to do all night. And according to producer Hidemaro Fujibayashi, that meant a ton of extra work, especially for him.

"I reviewed every single text of the NPCs," Fujibayashi told GameSpot. "And before, in the original game, each NPC didn't have a strict 24-hour routine, but in this game, they do. The director said, 'We want to have a 24-hour routine for every NPC.' And in my mind, I was like, 'That's going to be a lot of work.' [laughs] And I told them, 'That's going to be a lot of work,' but they said they want to do it. So in my heart, I was like, 'Okay, I guess I'm committed.'

"Because on the one hand, I know it's going to be a lot of work, but I also didn't want to discourage the young staff from coming up with new ideas and taking on new challenges," he continued. "So I had to roll up my sleeves and, on a daily basis, try to check as much of the dialogue as possible, working with the team, discussing what can be tweaked, what can be adjusted. So all of that to say that it was a lot of work."

The idea of a younger generation coming up with new ideas to modernize Ocarina of Time was a repeated theme during our wide-ranging interview with producers Eiji Aonuma and Hidemaro Fujibayashi, as well as how the more experienced developers would push the younger class to rethink their assumptions.
Ocarina of Time is enjoying stellar reviews across the board, including in GameSpot's 9/10 review . Currently it is also the top-rated game of 2026 on GameSpot sister site Metacritic.

articles.headline: Linux Mint 27 arrives next month, and I like it already: New features and other upgrades to expect
keyFacts: Linux Mint 27 is scheduled for release next month and features a new annual release cycle.
The update introduces several new tools, including the Superlight system monitor, the Unfold archive manager, and a new terminal application called Velocitty.
Developers implemented a dedicated hibernation feature and updated the operating system foundation to Ubuntu 26.04 LTS.
body: ZDNET’s key takeaways
- After a year in the works, the latest Mint is a complete refresh.
- It includes an improved Nemo file manager and a new system monitor app.
- It will also come with many updated programs, such as the GIMP image editor.
Linux Mint, my favorite Linux desktop distribution, is ready for a fresh start.

Its lead developer, Clement “Clem” Lefebvre, announced earlier this year that the team behind it was considering slowing Mint’s release cadence because the old twice-a-year release cycle was time-consuming and constrained their ability to make major changes. So it is that the next release, Linux Mint 27, will appear in your Christmas stocking.
More from ZDNET

The developers officially changed the designation on Oct. 13th when Mint changed both its release cadence and its numbering. Clem’s happy about the change: it “was a tough decision to make, but we’re really starting to see it pay off. We’re taking on projects and implementing changes which would previously have been considered too large or ambitious.”
Why Mint 27 rather than Mint 24?

Earlier development snapshots had been labeled Mint 23 “Alfa.” That title was explicitly a placeholder while the team decided its release strategy. Its final name is Adrien. Moving ahead, release numbers will be based on the upcoming year. Clem said, “We’ll no longer use point releases, so the release after that will be 28. You’ll upgrade from 27 to 28 to 29, and so on.” Instead of girls’ names, Mint will use boys’ names for distro titles.
The biggest changes

On Halloween, Clem announced the top changes in Mint 27. It starts with Mint bringing hibernation back into its supported desktop configuration through a dedicated Sleep Modes page in its System Administration tool. The page is intended to make enabling and configuring hibernation easier, including addressing its swap-space requirements.

It may not sound like much, but Clem explained it’s actually rather a big deal. “When you close the lid of your laptop, it goes into a sleep mode called “Suspend”. This mode is very useful… but it has a major limitation: It uses power.” People often forget it’s not really off and that your laptop will eventually run out of power. When that happens, “the outcome is worse than a normal shutdown. The session is gone, and the battery is empty.”

That’s where “Hibernation comes into play. It saves the session to disk and completely shuts down the computer. No power is used. When you reopen the lid, the session is as it was, and so is the battery.”
Superlight: System monitoring and storage analysis

Another new feature is Superlight. This fresh system-monitoring application replaces the older GNOME System Monitor. It comes with CPU, RAM, swap, GPU, network, disk I/O, temperature, and fan-speed graphs. It also includes per-application and per-process resource views. Battery-equipped systems also get charge and power-flow history.

Its storage analysis is particularly interesting: it can break down disk usage into files and folders, Steam games, and Flatpak applications. That brings several common troubleshooting tasks — “What’s using the CPU?” and “Where did my disk space go?” — into one interface. I’ve been checking it out on a Mint virtual machine (VM), and I like it already.
Cinnamon’s Nemo file manager gains a preview pane

The Nemo file manager is getting a media preview pane, toggled with F7 or a status-bar button. It supports pictures, audio, and video, and displays associated information — for photographs, that can include the capture date and camera model. I like this feature a lot. I’ve always done a lot of work from file managers going all the way back to the classic Norton Commander and its Linux successor, Midnight Commander.
Velocitty: a new terminal with practical session management

I’ve said it before, I’ll say it again. You don’t need to ever touch a Linux shell via a terminal to use Mint. But if, like me, you’re an old-school Linux user and you like using the terminal, Velocitty, Mint’s new terminal application, looks interesting. Its announced features include:
- A graphical tab overview and configurable color palettes.
- Tabs that can be reordered, moved between windows, or detached.
- Configurable shells and startup commands.
- Named, color-coded custom tabs with preset commands and optional automatic opening.
- Context-sensitive tab colors: red for elevated privileges, blue for remote sessions, and a lighter shade for running processes.
The point is to make recurring projects and SSH sessions easier to find and reopen. If you like other terminal programs, my latest fave is the Rust-based WexTerm; you don’t have to use Velocitty.
Unfold: a simpler archive manager

Unfold is a new archive manager for viewing, creating, and extracting archives. It uses 7-Zip and 7zip-RAR and supports the encryption formats those backends handle, including password-protected archives. Its design goal is simplicity rather than a sprawling feature set.
Under the hood: Ubuntu base, installer, and Wayland

The new Mint uses Ubuntu 26.04 LTS as its foundation. Mint is also moving from Ubiquity to the Linux Mint Debian Edition live installer for installing the operating system. This fresh installer comes with support for OEM bulk-produced installations, installation on both BIOS and EFI PCs, support for Secure Boot, and LVM/LUKS configurations.
For the Linux kernel, Mint 27 will use version 7.0. Which one exactly? Good question. We’ll see closer to Christmas.
Wayland compatibility remains the goal, but X11 isn’t disappearing. As Clem said in June, “In an ideal scenario, we manage to make Wayland work just as well as X11.” But they’re not there yet.
What makes this release different?

The central change is a cleanup of existing code. Mint’s longer cycle gives developers room to overhaul several parts of the desktop together, rather than squeezing individual improvements into six-month windows. As Clem put it in the September newsletter, “I don’t think I’ve ever seen so many changes and new features implemented for a single release.”

What that means for you and me will be better laptop power management, more capable built-in utilities, and a more complete collection of everyday desktop applications. For example, I expect the updated Mint will ship with GIMP 3.2.2 as its default photo editor, instead of Mint 22.3’s years-old GIMP 2.10.
